# Power Management

## Overview

Power management is a critical subsystem of the Aurora Nova Widget v2 beta unit, an open-source soil moisture and temperature sensor utilizing the MeshSync local mesh protocol without mandatory cloud dependence.  While marketing materials claim a 2-year battery life, engineering estimates project a maximum life of 18 months assuming a 10-node deployment.

## Key Details

The current power budget for the Aurora Nova Widget v2 beta unit is outlined as follows:

| Mode | Current | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| Sleep | 4.2 µA | Target |
| Sample + TX | 12 mA peak | 15 min interval |
| Rejoin spike | **110–340 µA** | Known issue |

- **Aurora Nova Widget v2:** The open-source soil moisture and temperature sensor hosting this power configuration.

## Related Concepts

- **MeshSync:** The local mesh networking protocol used by the widget (supporting a theoretical maximum of 32 nodes, though beta testing has been unstable at 8 nodes).
- **Parent Election:** A network formation process whose mechanism is currently undetermined ("??? (see whiteboard)").
- **Power Budget:** The planning document and metric tracking for current draw across sleep, sampling, and rejoin states.

## Contradictions

> **Contradiction:** There is a discrepancy in projected battery longevity between departments. Marketing claims a 2-year battery life for the dual CR2032 setup, whereas engineering estimates limit the lifespan to 18 months at a 10-node scale.
